entities.name: 4-methyl-3-cyanonitrobenzene
observations: The decoded substrate is a methyl cyano nitrobenzene; the nitro group is represented by the N-bound two-oxygen motif.
Exact positional naming is uncertain from the compact SELFIES representation.

entities.name: cyano-toluidine
observations: The product is the corresponding aryl amine, formed by replacing the aromatic nitro group with NH2 while retaining methyl and nitrile substituents.

entities.name: Aryl nitro reduction to aniline
observations: The reaction is a nitro-group reduction: aromatic NO2 is converted to NH2, with the nitrile retained.
The database does not establish a unique temperature, time, or isolated yield for this exact transformation.

entities.name: SnCl2 protic-acid reduction
observations: Tin(II) chloride is the strongest matched reagent precedent; records include aqueous or acidic media and ethanol, with acidic or ammonium-based workup components.
A practical likely variant is SnCl2·2H2O in EtOH with aqueous HCl or AcOH, followed by basification.

entities.name: Iron protic-acid reduction
observations: Iron metal is a second supported reagent class; records include Fe with ethanol and/or acetic acid, followed by workup.
A practical likely variant is Fe powder in AcOH/EtOH or Fe/NH4Cl in aqueous ethanol.
